title: San Mateo 1031 Exchange Coordination
name: San Mateo 1031 Exchange Coordination
metaTitle: San Mateo 1031 Exchange Coordination | San Jose, CA
metaDescription: 1031 exchange coordination for San Mateo's Bay Meadows office and multifamily, B Street retail, and fintech-anchored office space along the 101 corridor.

sections.html: San Mateo carries a more varied commercial base than most Peninsula towns its size, built on the redevelopment of the old Bay Meadows racetrack, a cluster of fintech and insurance-technology office tenants, and a downtown retail strip along B Street that has held up better than many comparable corridors. An exchanger identifying San Mateo replacement property is usually choosing between very different asset types under one roof of a city, and the underwriting approach changes meaningfully depending on which of those categories the candidate falls into. The city's position at the junction of Highway 101 and Highway 92 also makes it a natural crossing point between the Peninsula and the East Bay via the San Mateo Bridge, and that connectivity supports demand across office, multifamily, and retail alike rather than favoring any single asset class.

sections.heading: Bay Meadows and the Redevelopment of a Former Racetrack
sections.html: The Bay Meadows site, once home to a horse racing track, has been rebuilt over the past two decades into a mixed-use district of office, multifamily, and small retail, and much of the commercial product there is newer than the rest of San Mateo's building stock. Office space in Bay Meadows tends to serve mid-size tenants rather than the large single-tenant campuses found closer to the airport, and a buyer identifying this product should confirm build-out condition and remaining lease term carefully, since newer construction here still carries meaningfully different tenant improvement allowances than the legacy office stock elsewhere in San Mateo.

sections.heading: Fintech and Insurtech Office Demand Along the 101 Corridor
sections.html: San Mateo has built a concentration of fintech and insurance-technology tenants along Highway 101, and office buildings serving this tenant base tend to see shorter lease terms and more frequent expansion or contraction than legacy corporate tenants elsewhere on the Peninsula. A replacement property buyer evaluating this office product should review the tenant's headcount trajectory and funding stage where that information is available, since a fast-growing tenant may need to renegotiate space requirements well before its lease term naturally expires. A tenant that has recently downsized or paused hiring can also leave a building with sublease space on the market, which affects effective rent even when the headline lease appears fully occupied on paper.

sections.heading: Transit-Oriented Multifamily Near the Caltrain Station
sections.html:
Multifamily development near the San Mateo Caltrain station has leaned into transit-oriented density, and buildings here generally command a rent premium over comparable product farther from the station. A diligence file for a San Mateo transit-village multifamily property typically includes:

  • Trailing rent roll with unit mix and turnover history
  • Confirmation of parking ratio against current zoning requirements
  • Caltrain and bus proximity documentation supporting rent premium claims
  • Seismic retrofit records for any pre-1990s construction
  • Utility and capital expenditure history
  • Phase I environmental site assessment

Buildings without dedicated parking sometimes carry higher vacancy risk among tenants who still commute by car, so a buyer should not assume transit proximity alone guarantees full occupancy.

sections.heading: Retail Along B Street and at Hillsdale
sections.html: Downtown retail along B Street has kept a mix of independent restaurants and small local retailers, while the Hillsdale corridor further south carries larger-format retail serving a broader trade area. These two retail environments draw different tenant profiles and different lease structures, and a buyer should not assume the underwriting approach for a B Street storefront transfers cleanly to a Hillsdale-area retail building. A buyer should also confirm parking availability separately for each corridor, since B Street relies more on street and municipal lot parking while Hillsdale-area retail typically carries dedicated surface lots sized for a regional draw.

sections.heading: 45-Day and 200% Rule Strategy for Multi-Asset-Class Portfolios
sections.html: Because San Mateo offers office, multifamily, and retail replacement property within the same city, exchangers here often use the 200% rule to identify candidates across more than one asset class, keeping flexibility if financing or diligence eliminates one category before the 45-day deadline. The qualified intermediary should confirm each identified property description matches the specific building and unit or suite, not a general category, since a vague description can jeopardize the identification. This content describes process and coordination only, and exchangers should confirm gain treatment and depreciation recapture with a tax advisor before closing.

faqs.q: What kind of office product does Bay Meadows offer as replacement property?
faqs.a: Bay Meadows redevelopment has produced newer mid-size office buildings, generally serving smaller tenants than the large single-tenant campuses found elsewhere in San Mateo, with tenant improvement allowances that reflect that newer construction.

faqs.q: Why do fintech-anchored office leases in San Mateo carry more risk?
faqs.a: Fintech and insurtech tenants along the 101 corridor tend to sign shorter leases and grow or shrink faster than legacy corporate tenants, so reviewing a tenant's headcount trajectory matters more here than in a stable single-tenant building.

faqs.q: Does proximity to Caltrain guarantee full occupancy for multifamily?
faqs.a: Not automatically. Buildings without dedicated parking can see higher vacancy among car-commuting tenants, so transit proximity should be weighed alongside parking ratio rather than assumed to guarantee demand on its own.

faqs.q: Are B Street and Hillsdale retail comparable as replacement property?
faqs.a: No. B Street is an independent-restaurant and small-retailer downtown corridor, while Hillsdale serves a broader trade area with larger-format retail, and each carries a different tenant profile and lease structure.

faqs.q: Why would I identify across multiple asset classes in San Mateo?
faqs.a: Because the city offers office, multifamily, and retail replacement property in the same market, many exchangers use the 200% rule to name candidates across categories, preserving flexibility if one option falls through before the 45-day deadline.
